topology: synthetic remote peer and synthetic RUE run as independent JAIN SIP stacks on loopback
remote peer sends a real SIP INVITE containing the arm-specific SDP offer
RUE preserves the offer bytes it actually receives
RUE returns a real 200 OK containing the arm-specific SDP answer
remote peer preserves the answer bytes it actually receives and sends ACK
no RTT datagram is originated by this negotiation-only execution
an independent Python reducer parses the preserved offer/answer instead of trusting Java configuration flags
requiredFacts: remote T.140 capability is derived from preserved offer SDP
answer acceptance is derived from preserved answer SDP and treats port-zero m=text as rejected
the manipulated local RTT policy remains an independent test input
rttNegotiated=true occurs only in the both-enabled arm
Java is explicitly not verdict authority

provesOnly: the controlled RTT negotiation arms can be exercised through real JAIN SIP offer/answer dialogs
the independent reducer can distinguish absent, rejected, and active T.140 SDP states from captured bytes
successful T.140 SDP negotiation remains insufficient for RTT readiness without observed T.140 media
doesNotEstablish: a standards requirement to disable RTT in a session
